issues.legal_issue: Property tax on land leased to a tenant who constructs a building is assessed on the land and building together, with primary liability resting on the lessor of the land, unless the case falls within the statutory exception for qualifying long-term leases.
material_facts: The landowner had leased the plot to a tenant on a monthly basis.
The tenant had constructed a tiled house on the plot at the tenant’s own cost.
The municipal corporation assessed the land and house together and imposed primary liability on the landowner.
The lease did not fall within the provision applying where land is let for a term exceeding one year and the tenant builds on it.
issues.conclusion: The Act contemplated a composite assessment of the land and building, and the landowner was primarily liable for the property tax as lessor of the land.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 146(1) and 146(2)(a) of the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, premises let to a tenant are generally assessed as a composite unit, and the lessor of the land is primarily liable even where the tenant constructed the building. Section 146(3), which separately refers to land and building and provides an exception for qualifying leases exceeding one year, informs the interpretation of section 146(2)(a). Section 147 permits the lessor to recover the appropriate amount from the tenant and reflects the legislative purpose of facilitating tax collection. Sections 154–156 support the assessment scheme. The Court approved Ramji Keshavji v. Municipal Corporation for Greater Bombay, 56 Bom. L.R. 1132.

rule.if: municipal_property_tax_case and land_leased_to_tenant and tenant_built_on_land and lease_not_over_one_year

predicates.municipal_property_tax_case: The proceeding concerns the assessment or collection of municipal property tax.
predicates.land_leased_to_tenant: The landowner leased the land to a tenant.
predicates.tenant_built_on_land: The tenant constructed a building on the leased land.
predicates.lease_not_over_one_year: The lease did not exceed one year.

issues.definition: When a municipal property-tax case concerns land leased to a tenant who built on it, and the lease did not exceed one year, the land and building are assessed together and the land lessor bears primary liability.

issues.legal_issue: A long-standing administrative construction of an unclear statutory provision may support leaving that construction undisturbed.
material_facts: The Court assumed, in the alternative, that the statutory language could be read as placing primary tax liability on the tenant who constructed the building.
The municipal authorities had for a long period treated the land and tenant-built structure as a single unit and charged the tax to the landowner in such cases.
The appeal challenged the construction previously adopted by the High Court.
issues.conclusion: Even on the assumption that the statutory meaning was obscure, the Court would not interfere with the established construction supported by the authorities’ long-standing practice.
issues.legal_principle: Where an enactment is obscure, the Court may consider its contemporary construction as evidenced by long-standing official usage and conduct, expressed by the maxim optima legum interpres est consuetudo. The Court relied on Ohlson’s case, [1891] 1 Q.B. 485, 489, and Clyde Navigation Trustees v. Laird, 8 A.C. 658, 670, while recognizing that practice does not bind a court to perpetuate a mistaken interpretation.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_statutory_interpretation and statutory_meaning_unclear and longstanding_municipal_practice and existing_interpretation_matches_practice

predicates.appeal_challenging_statutory_interpretat: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an interpretation of a statutory provision.
predicates.statutory_meaning_unclear: The statutory language is capable of more than one reasonable interpretation.
predicates.longstanding_municipal_practice: The relevant municipal authorities followed the same construction through their usage and conduct for a long period.
predicates.existing_interpretation_matches_practice: The interpretation under challenge accords with the authorities’ long-standing practice.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an unclear statutory interpretation and that interpretation accords with long-standing municipal practice, the existing interpretation is left undisturbed.
